questions.question: What is the main difference in purpose between the tests in ⟨62⟩ and the enumeration tests in ⟨61⟩?

options.A: To quantitatively enumerate the total number of all mesophilic aerobic bacteria and fungi in the product
options.B: To determine the sterility of sterile injectable products only, for final release
options.C: To determine the absence, or the limited occurrence, of specified microorganisms
options.D: To evaluate the antimicrobial efficacy of the active ingredient in the product against various microorganisms

questions.explanation: The tests in ⟨62⟩ are used to determine the absence or limited occurrence of specified microorganisms, and thereby whether a substance or preparation complies with an established specification for microbiological quality. Quantitative enumeration of the total microbial count is the purpose of ⟨61⟩.
questions.reference: USP ⟨62⟩ Tests for Specified Microorganisms › Introduction

questions.question: What are the inoculation and incubation conditions for the inhibitory test of a culture medium, and what is the acceptance criterion?

options.A: Inoculate at least 100 cfu, incubate for not less than the longest period specified in the test, and no growth of the test microorganism is allowed
options.B: Inoculate not more than 100 cfu, incubate for not more than the shortest period specified in the test, and growth of the test microorganism must occur
options.C: Inoculate not more than 100 cfu, incubate for not less than the longest period specified in the test, and growth of the test microorganism must occur
options.D: Inoculate at least 100 cfu, incubate for not more than the shortest period specified in the test, and no growth of the test microorganism is allowed

questions.explanation: The inhibitory test is inoculated with at least 100 cfu and incubated for not less than the longest period specified in the test, and there must be no growth of the test microorganism, which confirms that the medium inhibits organisms that should not grow. It is the growth promotion test that uses not more than 100 cfu and the shortest incubation time and requires growth.
questions.reference: USP ⟨62⟩ Tests for Specified Microorganisms › Test for Inhibitory Properties, Liquid or Solid Media

questions.question: According to Table 1, which test strain should be used for the inhibitory test of Mannitol Salt Agar?

options.A: Staphylococcus aureus, because this medium is used to detect that organism
options.B: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, because it is paired with Cetrimide Agar
options.C: Salmonella Typhimurium, because it is paired with XLD Agar
options.D: Escherichia coli, to confirm that the medium inhibits organisms that should not grow

questions.explanation: In Table 1, growth promotion plus indicative testing of Mannitol Salt Agar uses S. aureus, while the inhibitory test uses E. coli. S. aureus is the strain used to verify that the medium supports growth and gives the indicative reaction; it is not the inhibitory test strain.
questions.reference: USP ⟨62⟩ Tests for Specified Microorganisms › Growth Promotion and Inhibitory Properties of the Media, Table 1

questions.question: What is the time limit for using a test strain suspension prepared in Buffered Sodium Chloride-Peptone Solution pH 7.0?

options.A: It must be used immediately and may not be stored, to avoid changes in the count
options.B: Use within 2 hours, or within 24 hours if stored at 2° to 8°
options.C: Use within 24 hours, which can be extended to 7 days if stored at 2° to 8°
options.D: Use within 8 hours, which can be extended to 72 hours if stored at 2° to 8°

questions.explanation: The test strain suspension should be used within 2 hours or, if stored at 2° to 8°, within 24 hours. None of the times in the other options is specified in the text.
questions.reference: USP ⟨62⟩ Tests for Specified Microorganisms › Growth-Promoting and Inhibitory Properties of the Media, Suitability of the Test and Negative Controls › Preparation of Test Strains › Aerobic Microorganisms

questions.question: In the suitability test of a new product, the antimicrobial activity of the product against a particular specified microorganism cannot be neutralized by any means. How should this be interpreted according to ⟨62⟩?

options.A: The test is invalid, and the test strain must be changed until that organism can be detected
options.B: The product fails, because it cannot meet the requirements of the suitability test
options.C: It can be assumed that the inhibited microorganism will not be present in the product, and no further action is needed
options.D: The enumeration method of ⟨61⟩ must be used instead, and the test for that specified microorganism is no longer performed

questions.explanation: The suitability test must be performed for each new product, and if the antimicrobial activity of the product requires a modification of the test procedure, neutralization or removal should be handled as described in ⟨61⟩. If the antimicrobial activity against a specified microorganism truly cannot be neutralized, it can be assumed that the inhibited microorganism will not be present in the product.
questions.reference: USP ⟨62⟩ Tests for Specified Microorganisms › Suitability of the Test Method

questions.question: What are the conditions and purpose of the pre-incubation for the test for bile-tolerant gram-negative bacteria?

options.A: Incubate at 20° to 25° for a time sufficient to resuscitate the bacteria but not sufficient to encourage multiplication, usually 2 hours and not more than 5 hours
options.B: Incubate at 30° to 35° for 18 to 24 hours so that the bacteria multiply in large numbers for subsequent detection and enumeration
options.C: Incubate at 42° to 44° for 24 to 48 hours to suppress the growth and multiplication of non-target organisms
options.D: Store at 2° to 8° for 24 hours to keep the bacteria in their most stable, non-multiplying state

questions.explanation: The sample is diluted 1 in 10 (at least 1 g) with SCDB and incubated at 20° to 25° for a time sufficient to resuscitate the bacteria but not sufficient to encourage multiplication, usually 2 hours and not more than 5 hours. The purpose is resuscitation, not multiplication.
questions.reference: USP ⟨62⟩ Tests for Specified Microorganisms › Testing of Products › Bile-Tolerant Gram-Negative Bacteria › Sample Preparation and Pre-Incubation

questions.question: For the Test for Absence of bile-tolerant gram-negative bacteria, what is the sequence of media and what is the criterion for compliance?

options.A: First MacConkey Broth, then subculture to Cetrimide Agar; yellow colonies mean failure
options.B: First RV Salmonella enrichment broth, then subculture to XLD Agar; red colonies mean failure
options.C: First Reinforced Medium for Clostridia, then subculture to Columbia Agar; rods mean failure
options.D: First Mossel enrichment broth, then subculture to VRBG Agar; no growth of colonies means compliance

questions.explanation: A quantity equivalent to 1 g of the product is inoculated into Enterobacteria Enrichment Broth Mossel and incubated at 30° to 35° for 24 to 48 hours, then subcultured onto Violet Red Bile Glucose Agar and incubated for 18 to 24 hours; the product complies only if there is no growth of colonies. The other options are media used for other specified microorganisms.
questions.reference: USP ⟨62⟩ Tests for Specified Microorganisms › Testing of Products › Bile-Tolerant Gram-Negative Bacteria › Test for Absence

questions.question: In the quantitative test for bile-tolerant gram-negative bacteria, in addition to the prepared pre-incubation fluid, which product quantities in dilutions are used to inoculate Mossel broth?

options.A: 1 g, 0.1 g, and 0.01 g, with results read from Table 2
options.B: 0.1 g, 0.01 g, and 0.001 g, with results read from Table 2
options.C: 10 g, 1 g, and 0.1 g, with results read from Table 3
options.D: 0.5 g, 0.05 g, and 0.005 g, with results read from Table 2

questions.explanation: The quantitative test uses dilutions containing 0.1 g, 0.01 g, and 0.001 g (or 0.1, 0.01, and 0.001 mL) of the product, which after incubation are subcultured onto VRBG Agar; the smallest quantity giving a positive result and the largest quantity giving a negative result are recorded, and the probable number of bacteria is read from Table 2.
questions.reference: USP ⟨62⟩ Tests for Specified Microorganisms › Testing of Products › Bile-Tolerant Gram-Negative Bacteria › Quantitative Test

questions.question: In the E. coli test, after 1 mL of the SCDB pre-incubation fluid is transferred into 100 mL of MacConkey Broth, what are the incubation conditions?

options.A: Incubate at 20° to 25° for 2 to 5 hours
options.B: Incubate at 30° to 35° for 18 to 24 hours
options.C: Incubate at 42° to 44° for 24 to 48 hours
options.D: Incubate at 30° to 35° for 3 to 5 days

questions.explanation: In the E. coli test, the sample is first incubated in SCDB at 30° to 35° for 18 to 24 hours; 1 mL is then transferred into 100 mL of MacConkey Broth and incubated at 42° to 44° for 24 to 48 hours, followed by subculture onto MacConkey Agar. "Incubate at 30° to 35° for 18 to 24 hours" is the condition of the preceding step.
questions.reference: USP ⟨62⟩ Tests for Specified Microorganisms › Testing of Products › Escherichia coli › Selection and Subculture

questions.question: In the E. coli test, suspected colonies grow on MacConkey Agar, but the subsequent identification tests are negative. What is the conclusion for the product?

options.A: It complies with the test, because the subsequent identification tests are negative
options.B: It does not comply, because any colony growth is judged as E. coli positive
options.C: It does not comply, unless it is re-subcultured onto Cetrimide Agar for confirmation
options.D: No conclusion is possible; a new 10 g sample must be taken and the whole test repeated from pre-incubation

questions.explanation: Colony growth only indicates the possible presence of E. coli and must be confirmed by identification tests; if there is no growth of colonies or the identification tests are negative, the product complies with the test.
questions.reference: USP ⟨62⟩ Tests for Specified Microorganisms › Testing of Products › Escherichia coli › Interpretation

questions.question: In the Salmonella test, what are the minimum sample quantity, the second-stage enrichment broth, and the subsequent selective plate?

options.A: At least 1 g; MacConkey Broth; MacConkey Agar
options.B: At least 1 g; Mossel enrichment broth; Violet Red Bile Glucose Agar
options.C: At least 2 g; Reinforced Medium for Clostridia; Columbia Agar
options.D: At least 10 g or 10 mL; Rappaport Vassiliadis enrichment broth; XLD Agar

questions.explanation: For the Salmonella test, at least 10 g or 10 mL is inoculated into SCDB and incubated for 18 to 24 hours; 0.1 mL is then transferred into 10 mL of Rappaport Vassiliadis Salmonella Enrichment Broth and subsequently subcultured onto XLD Agar. Suspected colonies are red, with or without black centers.
questions.reference: USP ⟨62⟩ Tests for Specified Microorganisms › Testing of Products › Salmonella

questions.question: In the P. aeruginosa test, how is the sample handled if the test article is a transdermal patch?

options.A: The whole patch is placed directly onto a 10 mL Cetrimide Agar plate and incubated for 18 to 24 hours
options.B: A sample quantity equivalent to one patch is filtered through a membrane, which is then placed into 100 mL of SCDB for incubation
options.C: Ten patches are ground up and inoculated directly onto a Mannitol Salt Agar plate for incubation
options.D: Half a patch is diluted 1 in 10 and inoculated directly into Rappaport enrichment broth for incubation

questions.explanation: For the P. aeruginosa test on a transdermal patch, a sample quantity equivalent to one patch is filtered through a sterile membrane, and the membrane is placed into 100 mL of SCDB and incubated at 30° to 35° for 18 to 24 hours, followed by subculture onto Cetrimide Agar.
questions.reference: USP ⟨62⟩ Tests for Specified Microorganisms › Testing of Products › Pseudomonas aeruginosa › Sample Preparation and Pre-Incubation

questions.question: On Mannitol Salt Agar, which colony appearance indicates the possible presence of Staphylococcus aureus?

options.A: Yellow or white colonies surrounded by a yellow zone
options.B: Red colonies, with or without black centers
options.C: White colonies with no color change around them
options.D: Colorless colonies surrounded by a green fluorescent zone

questions.explanation: S. aureus appears on Mannitol Salt Agar as yellow or white colonies surrounded by a yellow zone, and identification tests are still needed for confirmation. Red colonies with black centers are the appearance of Salmonella on XLD Agar.
questions.reference: USP ⟨62⟩ Tests for Specified Microorganisms › Testing of Products › Staphylococcus aureus › Interpretation

questions.question: In the Clostridia test, how is the prepared sample dilution treated before inoculating Reinforced Medium for Clostridia?

options.A: All of it is heated at 80° for 10 minutes and then divided equally to inoculate the enrichment broth
options.B: None of it is heated, and it is incubated directly under aerobic conditions for 24 hours
options.C: It is divided into two portions of at least 10 mL; one is heated at 80° for 10 minutes and cooled, and the other is not heated
options.D: It is divided into two portions of at least 10 mL; one is heated at 100° for 30 minutes, and the other is not heated

questions.explanation: At least 2 g or 2 mL of the 1 in 10 dilution (total volume at least 20 mL) is taken and divided into two portions of at least 10 mL: one is heated at 80° for 10 minutes and cooled rapidly, and the other is not heated. Both portions are inoculated and incubated under anaerobic conditions.
questions.reference: USP ⟨62⟩ Tests for Specified Microorganisms › Testing of Products › Clostridia › Sample Preparation and Heat Treatment

questions.question: What are the enrichment and subculture steps of the Candida albicans test?

options.A: SCDB incubated at 30° to 35° for 18 to 24 hours, then subculture onto Cetrimide Agar
options.B: Reinforced Medium incubated anaerobically for 48 hours, then subculture onto Columbia Agar plates
options.C: Mossel enrichment broth incubated at 30° to 35° for 24 to 48 hours, then subculture onto VRBG Agar
options.D: 100 mL of SDB incubated at 30° to 35° for 3 to 5 days, then subculture onto SDA

questions.explanation: For the C. albicans test, at least 1 g or 1 mL is inoculated into 100 mL of Sabouraud Dextrose Broth and incubated at 30° to 35° for 3 to 5 days, then subcultured onto Sabouraud Dextrose Agar and incubated for 24 to 48 hours; white colonies may indicate C. albicans and must be confirmed by identification.
questions.reference: USP ⟨62⟩ Tests for Specified Microorganisms › Testing of Products › Candida albicans
